# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the EXACT tasks you broke/fixed) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

<!-- cap-evolve:journal-append-below — add your Iteration entry under this line; do not edit anything above it -->

## Iteration cand_0001 — Code-enforce the four determinable rules (payment amount, baggage count, cancel eligibility, passenger dob), prose for the rest
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
  - tools.py `book_reservation`: normalize payment + passenger dicts, auto-fill the single-method amount to the exact total, enriched not-found/balance/does-not-add-up errors (cluster: booking payment/amount).
  - tools.py `book_reservation` + `update_reservation_baggages`: recompute `nonfree_baggages` from the membership×cabin allowance table (cluster: wrong baggage count, incl. task 12).
  - tools.py `cancel_reservation`: 2-layer eligibility guard — refuse if any flight flown; refuse if none of {within-24h, business, insurance, airline-cancelled} holds (cluster: cancelling ineligible reservations, e.g. task 37 IFOYYZ).
  - tools.py `update_reservation_passengers`: dob-alias normalization + count-mismatch enriched error (cluster: passenger-name correction). `update_reservation_flights`: payment-not-found now lists real ids.
  - policy.md: "basic economy is not a barrier to cancellation"; "if no condition holds don't cancel/rebuild"; "act only on the reservation asked about"; passenger dob-reuse rule; single-method pays full total (clusters: cancel confusion + wrong-reservation 17/22 + dob).
- Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe:
  - Payment normalization/amount-fill should fix task-8-style single-certificate books; safe because a correct single amount already equals the total (identity), malformed shapes are the only thing rewritten, and multi-method splits are still validated not auto-filled.
  - Baggage recompute should fix task 12; safe because a correct count maps to itself (verified all val gold counts recompute unchanged / to 0).
  - Cancel guard should fix task 37 over-cancel; safe because it fires only on policy-forbidden cancels — verified it does NOT block the gold cancels Z7GOZK (insurance) or K1NW8N (within 24h).
  - Passenger/dob + prose are additive restatements of existing hard rules; no new permission granted.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — this is the first iteration (LEDGER/RUNMAP/JOURNAL empty). Establishes the baseline cluster map + verified guards.
- Refuted hypotheses: none proven yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: wrong-reservation reasoning (tasks 17/22) — no safe code guard found (entangled with dialogue); only prose added so far. A composite "locate-then-act" tool or a confirm-the-reservation-id gate may be the lever if prose doesn't move it.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration: read this iteration's RESULT line — if the cancel guard or baggage recompute broke a passing task, relax the exact condition named; then attack tasks 17/22 with a composite tool rather than more prose.
